:::{#exm-bsc-capacity}
#### A channel that flips one bit in ten

For a [binary symmetric channel](#def-binary-symmetric-channel)
with $\epsilon = 0.1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
h(0.1)
&= -0.1 \log_2 0.1 - 0.9 \log_2 0.9 \\
&\approx 0.332 + 0.137 \\
&\approx 0.469 \text{ bits},
\end{aligned}
$$

so by @thm-bsc-capacity the capacity is

$$C \approx 1 - 0.469 = 0.531 \text{ bits per channel use}.$$

Each use carries one binary digit,
but on average only about half a bit of it gets through.
At $\epsilon = 1/2$, $h(1/2) = 1$ and $C = 0$:
the output is independent of the input.
At $\epsilon = 1$, $C = 1$ again,
since the receiver can flip every bit back.

:::
